description: LIKELY ROOT CAUSE FOUND for B28 NAE-28 cluster (AHU-3/4/6/7/11): B28 Secondary Chilled Water Supply Temp alarmed HIGH 46.6-47.6F on 7/3-7/4, sourced from JL-BLDG17-NAE20 Secondary Pump 1-2 (physically B17 Rm 1010). B28 has no local chiller plant - fed by this B17 secondary system. Same B17/NAE-20 location has cooling tower level alarms on Towers 12, 15, 16 (7/3-7/4) and DA tank near overflow (40-42in). Points to a capacity-constrained chiller plant at B17 as the actual source, not a B28-side fault. B28 AHU-7 hit 90.0F on 7/4 (worse than the 68.4F we tracked 7/2) - cluster kept climbing while unmonitored. NEXT: check B17 NAE-20 chillers 12/15/16 and secondary pump 1-2 status directly; this supersedes the earlier CWP-15 guess for B28 specifically (CWP-15 may still be relevant elsewhere, not confirmed which system it serves).

RELAPSE: improved to 68.4F on our 10:30 AM 7/2 check, then spiked back to 85.7F at 1:07 PM same day (alarm log). Whatever fixed it that morning did not hold - unit is unstable/cycling, not resolved. Needs re-check, not closed out.

UNRESOLVED 5-DAY PATTERN: 80.1F overnight DAT alarm recurring 7/1, 7/2, 7/3, 7/4, 7/5 - same value, same overnight window each time. Flagged days ago to check NAE-27 OAT sensor, never actually checked. Still happening nightly.

NEW THREAD: broad zone-temp problem across B51 SNE-03 - a dozen+ rooms (2600, 2610A, 2630, 2650, 2652, 2654, 2710, 2720, 2930A, 2950D, 2950E) hitting 78-91F daily/recurring. Rm 2600 specifically spiking 90-91F repeatedly. AHU-level discharge temps in this building have looked fine in DAT sweeps (AHU-3A/3B ~55F, PIV units cold). Mismatch suggests a DOWNSTREAM problem - VAV boxes, reheat, or zone dampers - not the AHU coils. Separate from the plant-capacity story, needs its own investigation.
